risks.if_unproven: priced as the model actually shown in photos (D3300), not the claimed D3400

risks.risk: Shutter count / sensor wear unknown, camera could have heavy prior use despite boxed appearance
risks.proof: Photo or screenshot of shutter actuation count from camera menu or third-party shutter-count tool

risks.risk: No proof camera powers on, takes photos, or that AF/shutter work
risks.proof: Video clip of camera powering on, focusing, and firing the shutter with a date/time stamp or spoken word

risks.risk: Lens functionality (VR, AF, zoom ring) unverified
risks.proof: Clip showing zoom ring moving smoothly, AF motor engaging, and VR switch toggled

risks.risk: Missing accessories (battery, charger, card, strap) not shown, box may be repurposed/empty

proof_requests: Close-up of the model name/plate on the camera body and a menu screen showing model/firmware info
Serial number photo on both camera body and box, side by side
Video of camera powering on, autofocusing, and shutter firing
Photo of shutter count from camera menu or software

response.reason: The seller explicitly claims the model is D3400, but every photo clearly shows 'D3300' on both the camera body and the retail box, a direct contradiction on the single fact that most determines price; this mismatch needs explanation before any valuation can proceed.
